feature: A moved layer stays under what covers it
summary: Dragging a layer that sits under another now keeps it under for the whole drag. Before, it was drawn on top until you let go, then dropped back under.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default.

try.do: Make a new blank picture and draw a rectangle with the Rectangle tool.
Draw an ellipse that overlaps part of the rectangle, and give it a different fill colour.
Press V, click the part of the rectangle the ellipse does not cover.
Drag the rectangle slowly under the ellipse and keep the button down.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Let go and watch whether anything changes as it lands.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

evaluate: While you drag, does the ellipse stay drawn over the rectangle?
Does the picture stay still when you let go, with no flash of the rectangle jumping under?
Does dragging still feel as quick as before on a big screenshot with a few marks over it?
rough: When something over the dragged layer mixes with what is under it (a blend mode such as Multiply, a lens, glass), or the layer is a piece inside a group with something drawn over it, the canvas draws the whole picture again on every move instead. That is correct but can be slower on a large picture.
Pixels lifted out of a picture with a selection and moved get the same fix, but no walk covers that case yet.
No mock covers this; it is how the canvas behaves while dragging.
